title: Week in Ripples, Sat 7 Nov: Nifty's best week since February 2021
description:
Hot topic: the Nifty and Sensex posted their best week since February 2021 as a seven-session rally lifted the Nifty above 25,000 on record foreign buying. Then: foreign flows, US payrolls, Asia's chip crash, oil, Wall Street, the rupee, Tata Steel, Hindalco and Muhurat trading.

1. Sensex and Nifty post their best week since February 2021 as a seven-session rally lifts the Nifty above 25,000 (Business Standard)
2. Foreign investors buy a record 45,960 crore rupees of Indian shares in a week as domestic funds sell a record 24,197 crore rupees (Business Standard)
3. US payrolls jump 165,000 in October, nearly triple forecasts, lifting December Fed hike odds to about 77-85% (Yahoo Finance (Reuters))
4. Asian chip stocks crash: Kospi halted after an 8% fall, Nikkei drops about 6%, SK Hynix falls 11.7% (Yahoo Finance (Fox Business))
5. Oil posts its biggest weekly drop since 2022 on Iran peace hopes, with Brent settling flat at 98.32 dollars (Rigzone (Bloomberg))
6. Wall Street steadies: Nasdaq gains 1.1% as AMD jumps 11%, but the S&P 500 still loses 2.7% for the week (Yahoo Finance (AP))
7. Rupee logs its biggest one-day gain since 12 October, closing at about 93.9 per dollar (IANS)
8. Tata Steel reports delayed September-quarter results on Saturday, alongside Divi's Labs, Tata Chemicals and HBL Engineering (PSU Connect)
9. Hindalco's profit jumps 59% to 7,533 crore rupees as revenue rises 39% to 91,708 crore rupees (Kotak Neo)
10. Diwali Muhurat trading runs on Sunday 8 Nov in a rare afternoon slot; markets shut on Tuesday 10 Nov (Outlook Money)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated with open-source Kokoro voices. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm P.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm S. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: It's Saturday, so this is our Week in Ripples. The big one: India's best market week since February 2021.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: S, how big a week are we talking?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty rose 8.57% for the week, and the Sensex 8.82%. That's the best week since February 2021.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: On Friday alone, Dhanteras, the Sensex jumped 1,718 points to 81,028. The Nifty gained 2.01% to 25,030, a seventh straight gain.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who moved?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Almost everyone. Only 4 of the 50 Nifty stocks fell on Friday. Banks led, with ICICI Bank up 4.75%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Mahindra and Mahindra was the top Nifty gainer, up 5.1%. HDFC Bank led the index, with banks at an eight-month high.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Fine, but 10% in seven sessions. Isn't that stretched?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. This rally is built on foreign buying, as money leaving the US AI trade rotates into India.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It takes the market into Sunday's Muhurat session and next week's CPI data with momentum, but yes, stretched.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So what do we watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The trigger: does the Nifty hold above 25,000 through Muhurat and Monday? A sharp reversal on profit-taking, or a weak CPI print, would test it.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Mahindra and Mahindra, and Reliance. Sentiment: positive.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: foreign investors set a record.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Foreign investors bought a record 45,960 crore rupees of Indian shares this week, including about 13,750 crore on Friday.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And the domestic funds?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: They sold a record 24,197 crore for the week. And foreigners are still net sellers of about 2.72 lakh crore for the year.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the rotation out of the US AI trade favours large banks and the rupee. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Axis Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: the US jobs report that changed the Fed math.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: US payrolls jumped 165,000 in October, against forecasts of about 59,000 to 70,000. Unemployment fell to 4.1%, and hourly pay rose 0.4% on the month.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And the Fed?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Odds of a December hike rose to between 77% and 85%, depending on the source. The 10-year yield rose about 2 basis points to 4.86%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a likely Fed hike on 9 December keeps the dollar firm, a headwind for flows into India. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: Asia's chip stocks crash.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: SK Hynix fell 11.7%, Samsung Electronics nearly 10%, and TSMC 8.5%. The Kospi fell more than 8% and triggered a temporary halt.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nikkei fell about 6% intraday, its worst day in eight months.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the sell-off tests the AI-capex trade behind India's electronics names. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Netweb, Dixon.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: oil's biggest weekly drop since 2022.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent settled flat on Friday at 98.32 dollars, but front-month futures fell about 13.2% for the week.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What's driving that?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Bloomberg reported US-Iran talks moving closer to a breakthrough. Saudi Arabia and the UAE have restored shipments, though Hormuz is not fully reopened.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: cheaper crude eases India's import bill, inflation and the rupee. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: BPCL, Indian Oil, HPCL, IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: Wall Street steadies. Sort of.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nasdaq rose 1.1% on Friday, as AMD jumped 11%. Intel gained 7.7% and Nvidia 2.8%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Why only sort of?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The S&P 500 still lost 2.7% for the week, its worst since June. The Nasdaq lost 3.4%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a partial rebound after Thursday's 5.5% Nasdaq fall eases the risk-off mood. Sentiment: mixed. What to watch Monday: whether US futures extend gains.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: the rupee's best day in weeks.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee rose 56 paise to 93.91 per dollar, its strongest close since 22 April, and about 1.2% higher for the week.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: IANS reported the RBI buying dollars near 93.88 to temper the move.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a firmer rupee lowers imported inflation but trims IT exporters' rupee earnings. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS, IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: a results Saturday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Tata Steel reports its delayed September-quarter results today, after postponing from 27 October. Divi's Labs, Tata Chemicals and HBL Engineering also report.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And Tata Steel shares?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: They were among Friday's gainers, going into the numbers.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Tata Steel's Europe losses and Indian steel prices set the tone for metal stocks on Monday. Sentiment: neutral. Stocks in focus: Tata Steel, Divi's Labs, JSW Steel, Jindal Steel.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: Hindalco's big quarter.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Hindalco's profit jumped 59% to 7,533 crore rupees, and revenue rose 39%. Novelis was the largest contributor.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: How did the stock take it?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Hindalco closed up 2.2% on Friday, at 958 rupees.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: strong aluminium earnings support metal stocks and help fund Novelis's expansion. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Hindalco, Nalco, Vedanta.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And story ten: Diwali Muhurat trading, at an unusual hour.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: NSE's Muhurat session runs tomorrow, Sunday 8 November, from 2:20 pm to 3:30 pm, breaking the usual evening slot.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Markets are then shut on Tuesday 10 November for Diwali Balipratipada, and again on 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a short, symbolic session and a mid-week holiday thin out trading in a CPI week. Sentiment: neutral. Stocks in focus: Titan, BSE, Kalyan Jewellers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch this weekend: Tata Steel's results today, the Muhurat close on Sunday, and whether foreigners keep buying on Monday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
